video.title: ESPN Points Mock Draft - Taking A Caleb Wilson Plunge

summary: Josh Lloyd does a 12-team ESPN points mock draft from pick 3, using ESPN default scoring, which penalizes missed field goals, missed free throws and turnovers. He criticizes picks that suit category or Yahoo formats rather than ESPN points, such as Durant, Barnes, Towns, Banchero and Castle. His team is Luka Doncic, Jalen Brunson, Evan Mobley, Deni Avdija, Ty Jerome, Damian Lillard, Jaden McDaniels, Caleb Wilson, Keegan Murray, Jakob Poeltl, Rui Hachimura, Nikola Vucevic, Paul Reed and a final-round upside flyer. His main lessons are to know your scoring format, avoid stacking injury and availability risk, and judge players by where you draft them compared with where they finish.

rules.text: ESPN default points scoring: made FG +2, FG attempt -1, made FT +1, FT attempt -1, a bonus point for a made three, and more points for steals and blocks than Yahoo default.
rules.quote: It's two points for a made field goal, negative one for an attempt, one point for a made free throw

rules.text: Know your format. ESPN points has a heavier penalty on turnovers and missed shots, so some category-league picks are reaches in this format.
rules.quote: There just plenty of other guys in this format where there's a heavier penalty on turnovers and miss shots

rules.text: Players valued for Yahoo scoring can be drafted too early in ESPN points. Understand the scoring before you draft.
rules.quote: he took Castle in a spot that makes sense for Yahoo, but does not make sense in ESPN. Understand your formats.

rules.text: Avoid stacking risky players on one team. Stacking several ifs makes it harder to succeed, even if the upside is real.
rules.quote: that's stacking risk. Now, there is upside that maybe both those guys are top 20 players.

rules.text: Value depends on draft spot compared with finish. A player drafted at 120 who finishes 120 is bad. A player drafted around 160 who finishes 120 is good.
rules.quote: Andrew Neard at 120 to finish. 120 is bad. Andrew Neard in round 14 to pick 160 to finish 120 is good.

rules.text: In the draft room, fill the positional slots first, then the flex and bench spots.
rules.quote: I always like to get those positional ones out of the way first and then fill the flexes in the bench after that.
